seo.title: Multiples of 11 Speed Grid - Double Digit Math Clicker
seo.metaDescription: Find all double-digit multiples of 11 from 11 to 99 on a 100-number grid. Fast-paced times table practice for 3rd and 4th grade math.
seo.intro: Under 100, multiples of 11 are instantly recognizable because they consist of repeated identical digits (11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99). On a 10x10 grid, these 9 numbers form a crisp diagonal line from the top-left to bottom-right. Spotting these symmetrical twin digits quickly develops visual pattern recognition and number familiarity.
seo.howToPlay: Scan the grid to click every multiple of 11 up to 100. Correct clicks lock green with a checkmark. Non-multiples flash red and deduct 2 seconds from the clock. Find all 9 multiples to earn 3 stars.
seo.teacherNotes: Show how multiples of 11 advance diagonally across the hundreds chart because each step increases by 10 (one row down) plus 1 (one column right).

faq.q: Why do multiples of 11 have repeated digits up to 99?
faq.a: Multiplying any single-digit integer n by 11 yields 10n + n, which places n in both the tens and ones columns (e.g. 7 x 11 = 77).

faq.q: How many multiples of 11 are between 1 and 100?
faq.a: There are exactly 9 multiples of 11 in this range: 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, and 99.
